title: Tune minimal polynomial path
description:
Tune the production minimal-polynomial path so the remaining SOTA target rows are closed by implementation work, not by unapproved exclusions.

## Background

The first implementation added a scalar Wiedemann front-end and closed the large-field rows, but several target cells still exceed the accepted fflas-ffpack reference by more than the epic's 1.5x wall-clock contract. This task now follows the attached no-exclusions implementation plan in `dev/active/d1dd266c-minpoly-sota-plan.md`.

The accepted reference rows are from `dev/bench_results/2026-05-04-c3e79272-minpoly-reference.csv`. The hard ceilings are:

| Cell | Hard ceiling |
|---|---:|
| `GF(2^31-1), n=64` | 2.519 ms |
| `GF(2^31-1), n=256` | 122.298 ms |
| `GF(65521), n=64` | 0.783 ms |
| `GF(65521), n=256` | 25.792 ms |
| `GF(251), n=64` | 0.202 ms |
| `GF(251), n=256` | 2.451 ms |
| `GF(7), n=64` | 0.854 ms |
| `GF(7), n=256` | 30.435 ms |

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Every in-scope `minpoly` target row listed above meets its 1.5x wall-clock ceiling on the current Zen 3 host, with no unapproved exclusions, **except for `GF(251)/n=64` minpoly per the 2026-05-07 amendment below.**
- [hard] `FieldMatrix::minpoly` uses a mathematically valid non-quartic production path for low-cardinality fields where scalar Wiedemann is unsafe.
- [hard] Packed prime-field matvec/minpoly sequence generation is used for the small and medium prime regimes where scalar row-by-row dot products cannot meet the target rows.
- [hard] Correctness is verified by adversarial and randomized tests: the returned minimal polynomial annihilates `A`, divides `charpoly(A)`, and matches an independent reference on small matrices.
- [hard] Throughput normalization remains aligned with the selected algorithm class per row (`n^3` for Wiedemann/cyclic/extension/block paths, `n^4` only for legacy reference fallback if retained outside production dispatch).
- [hard] Final evidence records raw wall times, gf2/reference ratios, algorithm class, and normalizer for every target row.

## Amendment — 2026-05-07 (user-approved)

Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-07: 7 of 8 minpoly target rows close on this issue's path. `GF(251)/n=64` minpoly remains at 2.84x (was 4.04x at d1dd266c open) — sibling task `70766cb1` reduced the gap by ~30% via inline panel-kernel + Barrett-table cache, but the residual constant-factor gap requires a bespoke register-scheduled small-prime AVX2 kernel in `gf2-kernels-simd`. That work is filed as **`52cce970`** (Bespoke small-prime AVX2 kernel for GF(251) charpoly+minpoly residual cells) and tracked under the broader finite-field LA SOTA catch-up planning issue **`615db3b9`**, NOT as a blocker on this issue.

Empirical basis for the amendment: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` § 3.1, § 6.1.

Re-escalation threshold: re-evaluate the GF(251)/n=64 minpoly cell when `52cce970` closes.

## Notes

The attached implementation plan requires validating the existing `cyclic_decomposition` LCM claim before using it as the deterministic cubic fallback. If that path is not correct for all adversarial cases, the plan proceeds through extension-field Wiedemann before escalating to block Wiedemann.
